expectations.text: A spec for the overdue feature exists under OUTPUT_DIR/repo/docs/product-specs/, either as a new file with a new prefix or as new criteria appended to tickets.md or cli.md with fresh IDs; the transcript or spec says which was chosen and why.
expectations.evidence: Created docs/product-specs/overdue.md with the new prefix `OVD` (OVD-001..OVD-008) and amended cli.md (new CLI-010; CLI-001, CLI-006 and the file intro amended). The why is in the spec's open question 8: 'Assumed: its own file, so that the goals, non-goals, and questions have one place.' questions.md Q8 says the same. Note: the repo's own guidance favors updating existing docs, and every other run in both iterations amended.

expectations.text: The spec has a one-paragraph intro, a `Prefix:` line, and a Non-goals section with at least two non-goals that are real boundaries (for example no notifications, no SLA pause on weekends, no change to the event log format).
expectations.evidence: One-paragraph intro: 'A ticket that passes its due time while it is still open or assigned is overdue. `ticketdesk list` marks each overdue ticket. `ticketdesk overdue` lists only the overdue tickets, earliest due time first. Support agents use both...'. 'Prefix: `OVD`.' present. '## Non-goals' heading with 7 boundaries (no notifications, no due-time change/business hours, no due-time display, no filters, no near-due warning, no new state or event kind, no late-close report). Also '## Goals' and '## Changes to existing specs' sections.

expectations.text: At least five criteria headed `### PREFIX-NNN: Title` with zero-padded three-digit numbers (a letter suffix such as TKT-014A is allowed), unique within the file; no `**Testable:**` lines. Body length is judged separately: most bodies are one to three sentences, and a longer body is noted, not a failure.
expectations.evidence: 9 new criteria: OVD-001..OVD-008 in the new file (check_run items=8, all new) plus CLI-010 in cli.md. Correct headings, unique, no Testable lines. Bodies 1-4 sentences; OVD-001 has an extra example paragraph. The shortest bodies of all twelve runs.

expectations.text: Criteria cover: the OVERDUE marker in `list` output; the `overdue` command's filter; the oldest-due-first order; a ticket exactly at its due time; closed tickets (either excluded, or an open question); and what the user sees when nothing is overdue (output and exit code).
expectations.evidence: Marker: OVD-004 'Each overdue ticket in it carries the `OVERDUE` marker' + CLI-006 line format. Filter: OVD-005 'returns every overdue ticket and no other ticket'. Order: OVD-006 'due time, earliest first... ID ascending'. Exact due: OVD-001 'overdue when ... the current time is later than its due time'. The boundary follows from the strict 'later than', but no criterion states the exact-due case outright; the explicit statement is only in open question 3 ('Assumed: no ... see OVD-001'). Passed because the criterion decides the case. Closed: OVD-002 'never overdue'. Empty: CLI-010 'With no overdue tickets it prints nothing and exits with code 0.' OVD-007 says only that 'the overdue listing is empty' (no output or exit code), but CLI-010 gives both. The exit code is also listed as an assumption in open question 6.

expectations.text: Every criterion body is behavioral: no function, class, module, or file names (such as TicketService, due_at, cli.py); outcomes are described as what the user sees in the CLI output or exit code.
expectations.evidence: No implementation names in new bodies (impl_words=0). OVD-008 'The log file is byte for byte the same' is an observable outcome.

expectations.text: The spec respects INV-001 and INV-002: overdue is a derived state computed from the ticket's due time and is not written to the event log; if the spec proposes a new event kind, it flags that as a change to LOG-002 and the invariants needing sign-off.
expectations.evidence: Intro: 'Overdue status is derived each time a command runs... It is never written to the log. This keeps INV-001 and INV-002 intact.' OVD-003: 'A ticket becomes overdue without any new event in the log.' OVD-008: 'append no event'. Non-goal: 'A new ticket state or a new event kind. TKT-001 and LOG-002 do not change.' Cites INV-001 and INV-002 by ID.

expectations.text: The spec does not contradict TKT-005 (due time by priority) or TKT-013 (listing order of `list`): it reuses the existing due time and states how OVERDUE interacts with the existing list order rather than redefining it.
expectations.evidence: OVD-001: 'The due time is the creation time plus the hours for the priority, per TKT-005.' OVD-004 states explicitly: 'The full listing still returns every ticket, sorted by ID ascending, per TKT-013.' Goals: 'the order of `ticketdesk list` stay as they are.'

notes: The only one of the twelve runs that created a new file: overdue.md with prefix OVD, 8 criteria plus CLI-010.
